title: Passive Voice
subtitle: Focus on the action or the receiver, not on who did it.
objectives: Form the passive voice (to be + past participle) in the present and past
Use the passive when the doer is unknown, unimportant, or obvious
Add "by" only when the doer is genuinely important information

content.intro: In an active sentence, the subject does the action ("The chef cooked the meal"). In a passive sentence, the subject receives the action ("The meal was cooked"). English uses this a lot when the doer doesn't matter.

rules.heading: Form
rules.body:
to be (in the right tense) + past participle.

  • Present simple passive: The cake is baked every Sunday.
  • Past simple passive: The house was built in 1990.

rules.heading: When to use it
rules.body:
• The doer is unknown: My phone was stolen. (we don't know who)
  • The doer is obvious/unimportant: The suspect was arrested. (obviously the police)
  • The action/result matters more than who did it: The bridge was built in 1930.

Add "by + doer" only if that information is genuinely useful: The painting was created by Picasso.

examples: The cake is baked every Sunday by my mother.
The results will be announced tomorrow.
The song was sung by a famous artist.
My car is being repaired right now.

commonMistakes.wrong: The cake is baking by my mother.
commonMistakes.right: The cake is baked by my mother.
commonMistakes.why: The passive needs "to be + past participle," not the -ing form (unless it's also continuous: "is being baked").
The passive always needs "to be" before the past participle.
Without "were," this isn't a complete passive sentence.

commonMistakes.wrong: The book was written by somebody.
commonMistakes.why: If the doer isn't known or important, just drop the "by" phrase entirely — don't force a vague "by somebody."

exercises.title: Fill in the Blanks
exercises.instructions: Complete each sentence with the correct passive form.

items.prompt: The cake ___ (bake) by my mother every Sunday.
items.explanation: Present simple passive: is + past participle.
Past simple passive: was + past participle (irregular: build → built).
Past simple passive, plural subject: were + past participle.
Future passive: will be + past participle.

items.prompt: The movie ______ directed by Steven Spielberg.
items.explanation: A finished historical fact — past simple passive, "was."
Present continuous passive: is being + past participle.

items.incorrect: The room cleaned when I arrived.
answer: The room was cleaned when I arrived.
items.explanation: The passive needs "was" before the past participle.

items.incorrect: The book is read by millions of people by someone.
answer: The book is read by millions of people.
items.explanation: "By millions of people" already names the doer — don't add a second, vague "by someone."

summary: Passive = to be + past participle, in whatever tense you need.
Use it when the doer is unknown, obvious, or less important than the action/result.
Only add "by + doer" when that information genuinely matters.
